title: Jad model.json
description: Session model and provider configuration. Secrets are referenced through an environment variable name, never stored here.

name.description: Display name of the model, shown beside its ID in the catalog editor. Changes no behavior; defaults to the ID.

provider.description: Provider identifier, for example openai or openrouter.

base_url.description: OpenAI-compatible SDK base URL. Do not include the /responses path.

api_key_env.description: Environment variable containing the provider API key. Not used when auth_mode is openai_oauth.

auth_mode.description: api_key reads the key from api_key_env. openai_oauth sends requests to the Codex endpoint with the access token read from oauth_auth_file; base_url is the endpoint and defaults to https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, so a proxy can be put in front of it. The backend only reads that file: sign-in and token refresh are done by a separate tool. Go backend: the expiry margin is the openai_oauth node of setting.json. The request body is the same as in api_key mode.

oauth_auth_file.description: Credential file for auth_mode openai_oauth; absolute or starting with ~/. Defaults to ~/.jad/auth/openai-codex.json. Not allowed with auth_mode api_key.

request.description: Additional Responses API generation options. The session runner owns model, input, instructions, stream, and tools.

instructions.description: Not allowed. Put the text in the profile's instructions: a model file is shared by every profile, so it is written once there. A model file that has the key fails to load.

efforts.description: Reasoning efforts a run may choose by writing the model as "<category>/<name>@<effort>" (the run body and a subagent's model; a profile's models and model_default list plain IDs). The chosen value replaces request.reasoning.effort for that run; without @ the request is used as written. An effort not listed here is refused. Absent or empty: the model has no choice and "@<effort>" is refused.

hosted_tools.description: Provider-side tool definitions sent after the function tools, for example [{"type": "web_search"}]. The provider runs them, so there is no tool code here; each object is passed on unchanged. The Go backend only; the TypeScript backend ignores it. Not supported by the Anthropic adapter, which refuses non-function tools.

type.description: Hosted tool type. function is refused; function tools come from the tool catalog.
